BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION

 IN THE MATTER OF THE APPLICATION OF EL PASO
 ELECTRIC COMPANY FOR REVISION OF ITS                                   Docket No. 25-00082-UT
 RETAIL ELECTRIC RATES PURSUANT TO ADVICE
 NOTICE NO. 317

 EL PASO ELECTRIC COMPANY,

        Applicant.


     EL PASO ELECTRIC COMPANY’S OBJECTIONS TO SUA SPONTE ORDER


       El Paso Electric Company (“EPE” or “Company”) has complied with the Sua Sponte Order

Vacating Procedural Schedule, Tolling Pending Deadlines, and Requiring the Filing of an

Amended Application (“Sua Sponte Order”) by concurrently filing an Amended Application that

complies with the requirements set forth in the Order. Nonetheless, out of an abundance of caution,

to identify concerns, and preserve the issues, EPE notes the following objections.

                                          BACKGROUND

       The background relevant to these Objections is as follows:

       1.      EPE filed its Application for Revision of Its Retail Electric Rates Pursuant to

Advice Notice 317 on March 27, 2026. The filing showed that EPE has a non-fuel base rate

deficiency in revenue of $70.6 million.

       2.      On April 15, 2026, after EPE identified workpapers that were inadvertently omitted

from the original filing, EPE voluntarily filed those workpapers as an attachment to its First Errata.

The First Errata also included three minor formatting corrections that were provided for the benefit

of Staff and intervenors. None of the corrections identified in the First Errata were substantive or

made a difference to EPE’s requested rate relief.
         3.     On April 24, 2026, the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission

(“Commission”) suspended Advice Notice 317 and ordered that a hearing be held concerning the

reasonableness of the proposed rates. As part of the April 24 Order, the Commission recognized

that EPE’s Application was “deemed complete as of April 15, 2026.” April 24 Order at ¶ 16.

        4.     On April 27, 2026, the Hearing Examiners issued a Procedural Order that would

allow the Commission to rule on the Application within the 9-month statutory suspension period.

        5.     Rate cases are complex and multifaceted proceedings with numerous issues,

multiple parties, technical pre-filed testimony on subjects ranging from finance, to accounting, to

engineering, and unlimited discovery. The contents of a rate case are governed by Rule 17.9.530

NMAC (“Rule 530”). The filing packages are complicated, constituting thousands of pages of

legal documents, pre-filed testimony, exhibits, schedules, and work papers. As the Commission

recognized, EPE complied with Rule 530 in its original Application.

        6.     Given the complexity, size, number of issues, and numerous technical calculations

comprising a rate filing package, changes and corrections are inevitable. See Sua Sponte Order at

¶ 26.

        7.     Since the Procedural Order was entered, EPE has received over 1,200 discrete

discovery requests. EPE has timely responded to those discovery requests, producing thousands

of pages of documents, over 1,200 answers, and providing a considerable amount of data to Staff

and intervenors.

        8.     As part of the normal discovery process, EPE identified four corrections. Rather

than wait for rebuttal to address these updates, EPE determined that it would be helpful and fair to

Staff and intervenors to identify the corrections before their Direct Testimony was due. EPE’s




                                                 2
 rationale was that by providing the updates early, Staff and intervenors would have the benefit of

those changes as they were developing their positions in the case.

       9.       EPE therefore filed its Second Notice of Errata on July 7, 2026, two weeks before

the deadline for Staff and intervenors direct testimony. Nothing in the Second Errata rendered the

original Application incomplete and the changes do not materially impact EPE’s proposed revenue

requirements. For perspective, the change to the proposed New Mexico Jurisdictional base

revenue requirement from the original Application is approximately $85,000 which amounts to

0.04% of the original revenue requirement.

       10.     Shortly after the Second Errata was filed, on July 10, 2026, the City of Las Cruces,

Doña Ana County, and the New Mexico Department of Justice filed their Expedited Joint

Objection and Motion for an Order Rejecting El Paso Electric Company’s Second Notice of Errata

and Staying the Procedural Schedule Pending the Company’s Compliance with NMPRC Rule

1.2.2.10(G) NMAC (“Errata Objection”). That Errata Objection was 15 pages long, was rife with

mischaracterizations and inaccuracies, and represented a fundamental misunderstanding of both

the substantive law and Commission procedure in rate case proceedings.

       11.     EPE was not allowed the opportunity to respond to the intervenor’s Errata

Objection. See Sua Sponte Order at ¶ 27.

       12.     Separately, on June 20, 2026, the City of Las Cruces filed its Verified Motion to

Dismiss El Paso Electric Company’s Application for Revision of Retail Electric Rates. Like the

Errata Objection, the Motion to Dismiss is filled with inaccuracies and mischaracterizations, and

lacks a sound legal basis.

       13.     On July 8, 2026, the Hearing Examiner issued an Order requiring EPE and Staff to

each file a written response addressing the Motion to Dismiss on or before July 21, 2026.



                                                3
        14.        On July 16, 2026, prior to that response deadline, the Hearing Examiner issued the

Sua Sponte Order. While EPE is confident that the Motion to Dismiss will be denied, as with the

Errata Objection, EPE was not given an opportunity to provide information or respond to those

filings before relief was granted by the Sua Sponte Order.

       15.        The Sua Sponte Order suggests that the Errata Objection “identifies a series of

specific facial inconsistencies, omissions, and unanswered questions concerning the Second Errata

Notice.” Sua Sponte Order at ¶ 13. EPE vigorously disputes this characterization, including that

there are any “facial inconsistencies, omissions, and unanswered questions” in its original rate

filing package.

                                           OBJECTIONS

       A non-exclusive list of EPE’s objections to the Sua Sponte Order are as follows:

       1.         The Sua Sponte Order orders significant relief that violate EPE’s procedural and

due process rights without providing EPE a meaningful opportunity to respond.

       2.         Although the Sua Sponte Order purports to be “sua sponte” it relies on unverified

allegations, incorrect assertions, and legal mischaracterizations from the Errata Objection and

Motion to Dismiss that EPE vigorously disputes. See Sua Sponte Order at ¶ 27. For example, the

Sua Sponte Order directs Staff to determine whether “the Amended Application resolves the facial

inconsistencies and omissions identified in the pending motions and objections.” Sua Sponte

Order at Ordering Paragraph G(8). EPE disputes that there are any “facial inconsistencies and

omissions” in its original rate filing package found to be complete by the Commission or that the

Errata Objection or Motion to Dismiss identified any basis for the requested relief. EPE objects

that it was not allowed to respond to the Errata Objection, the Motion to Dismiss, or the Sua Sponte

Order prior to being required to amend and refile its rate case filing package.



                                                  4
        3.      Similarly, the actions required by the Sua Sponte Order effectively grant the City

and County the relief they requested in the Errata Objection without affording EPE an opportunity

to respond or contest the unsubstantiated claims in the Errata Objection.

       4.      The intervenors have made a calculated choice to participate in this proceeding.

That participation comes with responsibilities, including conducting evaluations and analyses to

substantiate their case. EPE objects that the Sua Sponte Order requires EPE to conduct analyses

for the intervenors that intervenors should be capable of conducting themselves. See, e.g., Sua

Sponte Order at ¶ 14.

       5.      Although it does not identify the applicable standard, the Sua Sponte Order appears

to apply a mistaken standard to a rate case application that extends beyond the requirements for

rate filing packages for electric utilities in the applicable statutes and Commission rules.

       6.      EPE objects to the extent the Sua Sponte Order states or implies inadequacies in

the original rate filing package or prejudice to Staff or intervenors; specifically, EPE objects,

without limitation, to language, characterizations, conclusions, or implications in Paragraphs 13,

14, 15, 22, 23, 24, 28, 30, and 31.

       7.      Similarly, EPE objects to intervenor’s unsubstantiated conclusion, reflected in

Paragraph 30 of the Sua Sponte Order, that corrections identified in the First and Second Errata

are material to EPE’s Filing. In fact, the changes resulted in immaterial adjustments as compared

to the original Application. For example, the requested net revenue increase changed from $70.4

million in the original Application to $70.5 million in the Amended Application. For perspective,

the proposed New Mexico Jurisdictional base revenue requirement changed from $210,732,936 in

the original Application to $210,818,160 in the Amended Application, a difference of $85,224.

This amounts to 0.04% of the original revenue requirement.



                                                  5
        8.     EPE objects to being required to refile the entire rate package when more modest

action could have been ordered (e.g. filing a Bench Request).
